description:
Reconcile the workspace's field-capability surfaces — the FiniteField/ConstField hierarchy, the frozen PackedField/PackedFieldVec surface, generic batch operations, and per-field kernel selection — into a coherent set of canonical capability abstractions with offline, profile-driven kernel dispatch.

## Background

The workspace carries several partially overlapping capability surfaces: a two-tier FiniteField/ConstField trait hierarchy with a `Wide` delayed-reduction associated type; a user-approved, frozen PackedField/PackedFieldVec lane abstraction implemented by gf2-algebra; generic batch operations (batch inversion among them) as free functions in gf2-core; and kernel strategy selection embedded in field constructors and hidden dispatch hooks. Capabilities such as carry-less multiply, packed lanes, batch inversion, and canonical representation lack a coherent capability vocabulary, and backend selection is not driven by committed measurement.

This epic classifies each capability, names its one canonical abstraction, and cuts superseded variants over to it. Backend selection moves to a versioned, offline-generated tuning profile: calibration is an explicit benchmark action, and builds consume the committed profile deterministically. Proof obligations factor into algebraic laws stated once at the trait level plus per-backend representation refinement, keeping machine layout out of the mathematical specification.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An inventory classifies every field capability across the existing surfaces (trait hierarchy, packed lane abstraction, batch operations, kernel hooks, function-pointer dispatch) as an algebraic law, an algorithm, a representation refinement, or a kernel strategy, and names the single canonical abstraction for each with an explicit cutover for every superseded variant.
- [hard] REQ-02: Packed-capability placement resolves the gf2-core / gf2-algebra boundary: one crate owns the lane abstraction and the other consumes it, with no parallel definition remaining.
- [hard] REQ-03: Kernel and backend selection consume a versioned, committed tuning profile; host calibration is an explicit benchmark action rather than a build side effect, and unknown hosts select a conservative deterministic table with a tested scalar fallback.
- [hard] REQ-04: A pinned benchmark set with a predeclared non-regression tolerance passes before any reconciled capability trait becomes public API.
- [hard] REQ-05: Charon/Aeneas extraction of loop-free generic operations over the reconciled traits (the FiniteFieldExt::square / frobenius class) succeeds on the workspace MSRV toolchain, with proof obligations factored as trait-level algebraic laws plus per-backend representation refinement. Scope narrowed from a representative generic algorithm by owner decision DEC-A (2026-08-19): spike 34d85cb9 falsified extraction of F-carrying loops (finding F4, reproduced on newest upstream); the limitation is recorded in dev/active/34d85cb9/findings.md and its upstream report is tracked as issue 4dd5372a REQ-04.

## Notes

- The additive NTT epic is a planned consumer of the reconciled capability layer, deliberately without a dependency edge: it may proceed on concrete scalar types while reconciliation is underway.
- Existing surfaces to reconcile: FiniteField/ConstField (issue bfe0ba7b), the frozen PackedField/PackedFieldVec surface (issue 9fe275d3, locked at the gf2-algebra api-freeze), and the generic batch operations in `crates/gf2-core/src/field/batch_ops.rs`.
